q: The halting problem for cellular automata (does a given CA eventually reach an all-zero configuration from a given initial state?) is:
opts: Undecidable in general (for 2D or sufficiently complex 1D CAs)
Decidable if the CA is reversible
exp: The quiescence problem for cellular automata is undecidable by reduction from the halting problem of Turing machines, since CAs can simulate TMs. Even simple-looking CAs (like Rule 110) are computationally universal.
